item.title: Naviti Open Pro-Am set for October
item.description: GOLFERS will have another major event to look forward to when the Naviti Open Pro-Am is held at The Naviti Resort on October 17. The one-day tournament, organised in association with the Fiji Professional Golfers’ Association (Fiji PGA), is expected to attract professional and amateur golfers for a competitive day on the course.
item.content:encoded:
GOLFERS will have another major event to look forward to when the Naviti Open Pro-Am is held at The Naviti Resort on October 17.

The one-day tournament, organised in association with the Fiji Professional Golfers’ Association (Fiji PGA), is expected to attract professional and amateur golfers for a competitive day on the course.

The tournament will be played in stroke-play format, with the field limited to 70 players on a first-paid basis.

Registration will begin at 9am, followed by the shotgun tee-off at 9.30am.

The entry fee is $100 per player, which includes a buffet lunch.

Professionals will compete for $2,500, while amateurs will have the opportunity to compete for $3,000 worth of prizes.

Players wishing to take part must submit their registration forms by October 13, although late entries may be accepted subject to space availability.

The event also offers an opportunity for golfers to enjoy a competitive round while spending time at the Coral Coast resort.

A special accommodation rate of $395, including breakfast, is available for players wishing to stay overnight.

The Naviti Open Pro-Am is supported by VKM Dental Clinic.

With only 70 places available, golfers are encouraged to register early to secure their spots for the October tournament

item.title: Cullen to bring star power to CC7s
item.description: Former All Blacks star Christian Cullen will return to Fiji next year as the official ambassador for the 2027 McDonald’s Coral Coast Fiji 7s, while also becoming the 20th inductee into the RugbyTown Walk of Fame. Cullen, famously known as the “Paekākāriki Express”, will be honoured during the tournament’s 15th edition at Lawaqa Park, Sigatoka, from January 14-16, 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Former All Blacks star Christian Cullen will return to Fiji next year as the official ambassador for the 2027 McDonald’s Coral Coast Fiji 7s, while also becoming the 20th inductee into the RugbyTown Walk of Fame.

Cullen, famously known as the “Paekākāriki Express”, will be honoured during the tournament’s 15th edition at Lawaqa Park, Sigatoka, from January 14-16, 2027.

The former New Zealand fullback first made his mark in rugby sevens before establishing himself as one of the most dangerous attacking players in international rugby. He went on to earn 58 Test caps and score 46 tries for the All Blacks.

Tournament founder and chairman Jay Whyte said Cullen’s connection with sevens made his induction particularly significant.

“Before the world knew him as an All Blacks superstar, sevens provided a stage for that incredible speed, footwork and attacking instinct,” Whyte said.

He added that Cullen’s attacking approach had made him a popular figure among Fijian rugby fans.

Cullen will take part in tournament activities and engage with teams, supporters and the wider rugby community during his visit.

The RugbyTown Walk of Fame in Sigatoka recognises players who have made significant contributions to rugby sevens and the global game. Cullen will join 19 other rugby legends whose achievements are commemorated at the venue.

The 2027 Coral Coast 7s will feature 24 men’s, 12 women’s and 16 youth teams, with international teams competing alongside Fiji’s leading sevens players.

Organisers said the event would continue to offer free entry to Lawaqa Park, allowing fans to watch international stars, emerging players and rugby legends in action.

item.title: Women back on futsal stage
item.description: THE return of the women’s competition will be one of the major highlights of this year’s Bula Business House Futsal Cup, officially launched yesterday at Coffee Culture, Raojibhai Patel Street, Suva. The launch featured the official handover of major sponsorship from Design and Creative Building Solutions and Design Creative Scaffolding, as well as the pool draw for the 32 men’s and six women’s te
item.content:encoded:
THE return of the women’s competition will be one of the major highlights of this year’s Bula Business House Futsal Cup, officially launched yesterday at Coffee Culture, Raojibhai Patel Street, Suva.

The launch featured the official handover of major sponsorship from Design and Creative Building Solutions and Design Creative Scaffolding, as well as the pool draw for the 32 men’s and six women’s teams competing this year.

Event organiser Alan Kumar said the women’s category had been reintroduced following strong demand after it was not held last season.

“As you can see, last competition season, we didn’t have the women’s competition. So we have reintroduced after a lot of requests and demand,” Kumar said.

He said the return of the category would add another dimension to the tournament while creating an opportunity for women to compete and showcase their skills.

Unlike the men’s competition, the women’s category will have no entry fee, with organisers aiming to remove barriers to participation. “We are not charging any entry fees for the women because we believe there’s a platform where we give equal platform for women to compete alongside the men’s category as well,” he said.

The women’s competition will also be open to players outside the participating businesses, allowing teams to register players regardless of their employment.

“For the women, it’s open. That means anyone can come and play. You just have to register,” Kumar said. With between $3000 and $5000 allocated as prize money for the women’s category, Kumar believes the competition can become a pathway for talented players to progress into higher levels of the sport.

“From future, they can play at the national level and at the professional level as well,” he said.

item.title: Feni hat-trick lifts Suva past Navua
item.description: GLOBAL CARE Suva FC striker Gagame Feni’s hat-trick helped Suva overcome Blue Gas Navua FC 3-1 in their opening match of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday. Navua suffered a major setback when captain Thomas Dunn was shown a straight red card for using foul and abusive language towards match officials, forcing his side to play with 10 men fo
item.content:encoded:
GLOBAL CARE Suva FC striker Gagame Feni’s hat-trick helped Suva overcome Blue Gas Navua FC 3-1 in their opening match of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday.

Navua suffered a major setback when captain Thomas Dunn was shown a straight red card for using foul and abusive language towards match officials, forcing his side to play with 10 men for the remaining minutes of the second half.

Vanuatu import Feni credited teamwork for Suva’s comeback victory.

“I reminded the Suva boys to work as a team, work as a unit and play for each other.

“We knew the game would be tough. First games are always tough, but I just reminded them to concentrate,” Feni said.

Navua head coach RodickS Singh was frustrated with the result but remained determined to see his side fight for a place in the semi-finals in today’s second pool match against Nasinu, despite Dunn being suspended.

“Not the result we wanted, but disappointed with how we were treated in this game.

“If you look at it, Thomas Dunn getting a red card and the boys didn’t recover from it. Why he got the red card was an issue, and what incident led to him getting the red card is another issue.

“This loss is going to make us more hungry to make it to the semi-final. We lost a bit of momentum today with losing a player, but we will not back down,” Singh said. Navua started strongly and took the lead through Walter Leoru in the first half to go into the break 1-0 ahead. However, Suva regrouped after halftime and turned the match around, with Feni scoring all three goals to complete his hat-trick and secure the victory for Suva.

item.title: Another painful loss
item.description: The Vinod Patel Ba Men’s came unstuck against Malolo last week leaving them down in eighth place with a mountain to climb if they are to achieve their season’s goals. “That’s the third game we’ve lost at the death,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said, recalling the end-of-game slip-ups against Tailevu and Taveuni.
item.content:encoded:
The Vinod Patel Ba Men’s came unstuck against Malolo last week leaving them down in eighth place with a mountain to climb if they are to achieve their season’s goals.

“That’s the third game we’ve lost at the death,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said, recalling the end-of-game slip-ups against Tailevu and Taveuni.

Coach Ben Tora opted to give his regular front rowers a break after four games and started with three new faces.

Malolo capitalised on this and led 20-3 before top prop Allen Osborne and hooker Ben Sokia were introduced.

Osborne began with his second try in two weeks, while Sokia’s experience solidified the set pieces.

Once they got into their swing, Ba dominated play and scored three tries to lead 22-20 only to concede a painful late score after the hooter to lose 22-25.

With away games to Nadroga today and Nadi next week, Tora’s team need to step up and get some wins on the board before their run of four straight home games at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.

From 19 September, Ba host table-toppers Naitasiri then Rewa, Kadavu and Lautoka.

“We are not where we planned to be,” Kautoga admitted. “So there’s a lot of work to be done.”

item.title: Labasa stamp early authority
item.description: Defending 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants champions Labasa FC stamped their authority on day one of the tournament after edging Nasinu FC 1-0 at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday. The Babasiga Lions struck in the first half through Joseph Joe and held on firmly in the second half to secure all three points.
item.content:encoded:
Defending 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants champions Labasa FC stamped their authority on day one of the tournament after edging Nasinu FC 1-0 at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday.

The Babasiga Lions struck in the first half through Joseph Joe and held on firmly in the second half to secure all three points.

Labasa created several opportunities to extend its lead, but Nasinu’s young side showed determination and resilience to keep the defending champions at bay.

Labasa head coach Alvin Chand was satisfied with the result, admitting that defending the title away from home would be a tough challenge.

“We won in Labasa last year and this year we are here in Ba. It will be tough to defend, but we are looking forward to it.

“I thank my boys. We managed to get the three points. The first game is always tough in tournaments and the result can go either way, but we managed to get the win,” Chand said.

Nasinu head coach Abunesh Kapur was proud of his young players despite the narrow defeat.

“It was unfortunate, but I’m proud of my team. We have a young team, and six of them are U20 players,” Kapur said.

item.title: Houshmand and Brooks Fiji Pro champions
item.description: FIJI Pro 2026 champions Cole Houshmand and Erin Brooks stamped their authority on the World Surf League’s Pacific Leg, claiming memorable victories after a spectacular Finals Day at Cloudbreak on Tavarua Island yesterday. Cloudbreak saved some of its finest conditions for the final day, providing a fitting stage for two surfers in outstanding form to celebrate major victories and strengthen their
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Pro 2026 champions Cole Houshmand and Erin Brooks stamped their authority on the World Surf League’s Pacific Leg, claiming memorable victories after a spectacular Finals Day at Cloudbreak on Tavarua Island yesterday.

Cloudbreak saved some of its finest conditions for the final day, providing a fitting stage for two surfers in outstanding form to celebrate major victories and strengthen their positions heading into the final stretch of the Championship Tour season.

For Canadian star Brooks, the victory completed a remarkable Pacific Leg sweep and secured her second Fiji Pro title. Her triumph came after another impressive run at Cloudbreak, although the anticipated Final showdown with friend Isabella Nichols was denied after Nichols suffered an unfortunate injury during her semifinal.

Brooks’ success has lifted her to No.8 in the rankings as the Championship Tour now moves to Lower Trestles in Southern California. With valuable points still available, she remains firmly in contention to make a stronger push in the World Title race.

On the men’s side, American Cole Houshmand continued his extraordinary rise, claiming his third Championship Tour victory from three Final appearances.

The Fiji triumph added to his victories at Bells Beach and Brazil, further establishing Houshmand as one of the sport’s most dangerous competitors.

His Finals Day performance was nothing short of spectacular.

Houshmand produced a 9.43-point ride in the semifinals before delivering another outstanding performance in the Final against two-time Fiji Pro winner Gabriel Medina.
